descriptions.heading: What each metric means

main.title: ❤️ BPM — Heart Rate
main.text: Heartbeats per minute, estimated from the optical pulse in your fingertip. Typical adult resting range: about 60–100 bpm, often lower in active people. Caffeine, movement and stress raise it.

main.title: 🌬️ /min — Breathing Rate
main.text: Approximate breaths per minute, estimated from the slow rise and fall of the pulse signal. Typical resting range: 12–20. Shown only when a clear rhythm is found.

main.title: ⚡ Stress %
main.text: Experimental: 130 × CSI (how irregular your beat intervals look). A typical camera reading is around 40%. Strongly affected by movement and signal quality; not a validated stress measure.

main.title: 🔋 Energy %
main.text: Experimental: starts at 90% and drops as heart rate rises above 75 bpm and as the rhythm looks more irregular. A rough hint, not a measure of how energetic you are.

advanced.title: HRV surrogate (RMSSD)
advanced.text: RMSSD: root mean square of successive differences between beat intervals, in ms (capped at 100). Reflects vagal (parasympathetic) activity. Camera readings over 15 s are rough and often run high.

advanced.title: Cardiac Stability Index (CSI)
advanced.text: Standard deviation of beat intervals divided by their mean. Lower = more even intervals and a cleaner signal. Typical camera readings are around 0.3; clearly higher values usually mean movement or noise.

advanced.title: Recovery Rate %
advanced.text: How far the latest beat has come back from the highest heart rate in the last 15 s toward the window average. 100% = back at average; 0% = still at the peak, or no peak at all.

advanced.title: HR Trend Slope
advanced.text: Straight-line trend of your beat intervals over the window, sign-flipped. Positive = heart rate rising; negative = heart rate easing down.

advanced.title: HR Acceleration
advanced.text: Average change between consecutive beat intervals. Positive = intervals lengthening (pulse slowing); negative = shortening (pulse rising). Near zero at rest.

emotional.title: Alarm / Anxiety
emotional.text: Experimental: 0.7 × Stress plus a bump when estimated breathing is above 15/min. Rises with irregular-looking rhythm and faster breathing; not an anxiety test.

emotional.title: Relaxation / Calmness
emotional.text: Experimental: higher when the rhythm looks steady (low CSI) and Energy is high (pulse not above ~75 bpm).

emotional.title: Focus / Concentration
emotional.text: Experimental: average of Energy and inverse Stress. Highest with a moderate pulse and steady rhythm; it cannot measure attention.

emotional.title: Excitement
emotional.text: Experimental: rises with heart rate above 60 bpm (plus a little with breathing rate). Cannot tell excitement from nerves, effort or caffeine.

emotional.title: Fatigue
emotional.text: Experimental: rises as Energy falls and Stress rises, i.e. with a pulse above 75 bpm and an irregular-looking rhythm. Not a measure of tiredness.

emotional.title: Flow
emotional.text: Experimental: 60% Focus + 40% Relaxation. Higher with a moderate pulse and steady rhythm; it cannot detect a flow state.

descriptions.footnote1: All metrics are derived from the optical PPG signal via the device camera.
descriptions.footnote2: For medical-grade accuracy use a certified biometric device.
